ledger.claim: The driver was never at the booked pickup. The GPS arrival check on this trace returns corroborated = false: the nearest fix to the pickup inside the 120 s arrival window is 476.59 m away (fix at 08:04:50, reported accuracy 8.0 m, so it passes the 25 m accuracy filter and counts), against an arrival radius of 50 m for a STANDARD-class pickup. The driver pressed 'arrived' at 08:06:50 and the trace then holds him stationary at roughly half a kilometre from the pickup until cancellation. On POL-NS-21's own arrival test, the arrival event is not made out.

POL-NS-21's free wait is five minutes spent waiting at the pickup, and POL-NS-22 permits the 5.00 SGD fee only where the driver cancels after that wait. Here the wait timer started on a button press at 08:06:50 at a position the trace places 476.59 m from the pickup, and the fixes from then to the 08:19:10 cancellation all report 0 kph at that same stationary point away from the pickup. No free wait was served at the pickup, so the precondition POL-NS-22 attaches to the fee is not satisfied and the 5.00 SGD standing on the payments ledger cannot be kept.

POL-NS-24 applies on its terms: where the driver fails to arrive at the pickup location by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, any fee charged is refunded in full. The scheduled time is 08:10:00, the deadline 08:15:00 (derived driver_deadline, driver_late_after_scheduled_sec = 300), and the trace's nearest approach to the pickup is 476.59 m, so the driver had not arrived at the pickup by the deadline or at any point afterwards. The record's arrived_by_deadline = true is computed from the arrival button alone, which the GPS does not corroborate, so it cannot satisfy the test POL-NS-21 prescribes. That the driver cancelled at 08:19:10 rather than the rider cannot convert a charge the policy denies into one it allows; the clause's remedy is directed at the charge. The rider, as the filing party, asks FULL_REFUND of the whole 5.00 SGD contested amount, with no driver compensation.

The driver's own first message, MSG-05057-001 at 08:07:10, reads 'I reach already at Blk 215 carpark', while the booking pickup on the trip record is Block 251, Hougang Avenue 3. That is a counterparty statement in the chat log placing him somewhere other than the booked pickup; his later message at 08:14:00, 'I'm at the pickup point waiting already', gives no location at all, and his counter-statement that he 'was at the pickup point waiting more than 10 minutes' is contradicted by the platform's own trace. The driver's account of where he was is not merely unproven by him; it is contradicted by his own message and by the trace.

The rider presented at the booked pickup: her message MSG-05057-002 at 08:11:30, inside the free wait that ran to 08:15:00, states she was at 'Blk 251 drop off' and asks the driver where he was, and the driver never told her. The trace carries no rider track, so the rider's own position rests on that in-app statement; but nothing in the record places her anywhere other than the booked pickup, and the only location measurement in the case places the driver 476.59 m away. A no-show charge requires a driver who was there to be shown to; this record does not show one.

I do not contest POL-NS-23 on this record. The driver messaged at 08:07:10 and 08:14:00 and placed one in-app call at 08:15:20 (unanswered, 15 s), all before the 08:19:10 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met and neither FULL_REFUND under POL-NS-23 nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 — which requires that the driver also failed to attempt contact — is available on this trip. That does not save the fee: contact and location are separate obligations, the contact obligation is the one the driver met, and it is the location obligation that fails.

No escalation is open on this record. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established because the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired, and here the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 100% coverage, 47 fixes at the 30 s sample interval, no gaps, and a maximum gap of 30 s against the 120 s policy impairment threshold, and its derived arrival check settles where the driver was. The only impaired artifact is EV-ADVIS-05057-01, a traffic advisory whose status is MISSING with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0; it carries no fact, and no no-show rule needs a traffic record, so its absence leaves no rule element unestablished.

This is a case the AI decides. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and no fraud flag is carried by either party: driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0, and the rider profile carries no fraud flag (0 when the field is absent). POL-NS-26 therefore makes the AI ruling final on this no-show at any confidence, and there is no basis in POL-GEN-22 or POL-NS-26 for holding the 5.00 SGD instead of returning it to the rider who filed.

The driver's free wait had expired before he cancelled. POL-NS-21 fixes the free wait at 300 s, and because the driver marked arrival at 08:06:50 — before the 08:10 scheduled pickup — the wait ran from the schedule and ended at 08:15:00. The cancellation came at 08:19:10, 550 s after the wait opened and more than four minutes after it closed, so the driver was entitled to cancel as a rider no-show.

POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the driver neither sent an in-app message nor placed an in-app call before cancelling. Here the chat log carries two driver messages (08:07:10 and 08:14:00) and the trip record carries one in-app call at 08:15:20, all before the 08:19:10 cancellation, so obligation_met is true and POL-NS-23's FULL_REFUND is not engaged.

POL-NS-24 refunds a no-show fee only where the driver failed to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes — 08:15:00 on this trip. The trip record puts the arrival event at 08:06:50 with arrived_by_deadline true, well inside that deadline, and the cancellation is recorded as made by the driver, not the rider, so the driver-late ground for a refund is not made out.

Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 transfers it to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, with driver_compensation_sgd equal to the fee charged. The ledger shows a single cancellation line of exactly 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy true, driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd 5.00 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the fee stands in full and the driver is owed 5.00 SGD.

The rider filed this dispute, and the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and preserves the present payment state, so if the rider's claim fails the 5.00 SGD simply stands and the driver keeps it; a refund has to be positively justified by a clause that voids the fee, and none does.

Nothing in the record puts the rider at the marked pickup. The GPS trace carries no rider track at all, the driver's only in-app call at 08:15:20 went unanswered, and the platform's own wait timer ran from 08:06:55 and expired at 08:11:55 with the rider recorded as not on board; the rider's first message came only at 08:11:30. The no-show premise rests on the platform's own timer, which supports the driver's account.

The 50 m arrival radius is a corroboration test for the trip record's arrival event — an evidence procedure that issues no ruling value of its own, not one of the clauses that voids a no-show fee. The two clauses that can void this fee on the driver's conduct, POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24, both run the driver's way on the delivered record, so the rider's wrong-block allegation cannot by itself defeat a fee that POL-NS-22 otherwise licenses.

If the Tribunal is not satisfied that the driver's stopped position was the marked pickup point, the record leaves that fact open rather than resolved against the driver: the derived arrival check reports corroborated false and a nearest fix of 476.59 m, but pickup and dropoff both carry a null venue_id, the log contains no statement fixing the driver's stopped position at the marked point, and the trace carries no rider-side track to test the rider's claim that he was there either. POL-GEN-26 then requires the case to go to a human reviewer with the fee held, not refunded, because no outcome may be inferred from the absence of evidence.

The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD first band, and neither profile carries fraud_flags of 1 or more, so the confidence the AI ruling needs is nil and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on this no-show final. The Tribunal should rule on the fee, with escalation reserved for a POL-GEN-26 fact the record genuinely cannot establish.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 5.00 no-show fee charged on TRP-05057 is refunded in full to Ms Rider (R-78887); the driver receives no compensation.

Why the fee cannot stand. A no-show charge presupposes that the driver was actually at the booked pickup and waited there. Here the arrival test reads the trip record's arrival event against the GPS trace inside the 50 m radius for a standard pickup. The trace is complete and unimpaired (47 fixes, 100% coverage, 30 s sampling, no gaps), and it never puts the driver at the pickup: his closest fix is 476.59 m away (08:04:50, accuracy 8.0 m, so it passes the 25 m filter and counts), and from the 08:06:50 arrival press until the 08:19:10 cancellation every fix shows him stationary at 0 kph roughly 650 m from Block 251, Hougang Avenue 3. His own message at 08:07:10 says he is at 'Blk 215 carpark', not Block 251. The arrival button only records that he pressed it; the platform's own measurement contradicts it, so the arrival event is not made out and the free wait from the scheduled 08:10:00 to 08:15:00 was not served at the pickup.

Because the driver had not arrived at the pickup by the scheduled time plus five minutes (08:10:00 + 300 s = 08:15:00), POL-NS-24 applies on its terms: any fee charged is refunded in full. That is the SGD 5.00 single cancellation line on the ledger (EV-FARE-05057, fee_matches_policy true, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). POL-NS-22 does not help the driver, because its precondition — a cancellation after a free wait spent at the pickup — is not satisfied.

Points I considered and rejected. The driver's argument that the fee stands because the timer expired (POL-NS-21/POL-NS-22) fails: the timer is a party-set status, not a measurement, and the wait was not served at the pickup. His argument that arrived_by_deadline = true saves the fee fails for the same reason: that value is computed from the button alone and is contradicted by the trace. His NO_ACTION argument (POL-GEN-03) fails because a clause, POL-NS-24, voids the charge. I accept that POL-NS-23 (contact) is satisfied — two driver messages (08:07:10, 08:14:00) and one in-app call (08:15:20) all before the 08:19:10 cancellation — so no refund arises on the contact ground and no SGD 5.00 goodwill credit is due, since the driver did attempt contact; but contact and location are separate obligations, and it is the location obligation that fails.

Escalation is not open. POL-GEN-26 applies only where a needed fact cannot be established because its evidence is missing or impaired; here the trace is complete and the arrival check settles where the driver was. The only impaired artifact is the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05057-01, weight 0.0), which carries no fact and which no no-show rule needs.

Confidence and authority: every artifact carrying the deciding facts (EV-GPS-05057, EV-TRIP-05057, EV-CHAT-05057, EV-FARE-05057) has weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The contested amount is SGD 5.00, below POL-GEN-22's SGD 10.00 first band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag of 1 or more, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final at any confidence. No referral is produced by any clause: the fee is exactly SGD 5.00 (no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral), contact was attempted (no POL-NS-24 goodwill referral), and the rider's repeat no-show counter is absent and the fee does not stand (no POL-NS-25 referral).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
